content:
Background The Japanese financial industry generates vast amounts of documents—annual reports, earnings summaries, regulatory filings—that require both visual understanding and domain-specific reasoning. While recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have shown impressive capabilities in general tasks, their performance on Japanese financial documents remains limited due to the unique challenges of this domain: complex table layouts, mixed Japanese-English text, and the need for numerical reasoning.
In this work, we set out to build a specialized VLM that can not only read Japanese financial documents but also reason about their contents in a financially meaningful way.
Approach Our approach integrates two key components:
Reasoning Enhancement We employ a multi-stage training pipeline that progressively strengthens the model’s reasoning capabilities:
Pre-training on financial corpora: We curate a large-scale dataset of Japanese financial texts, including annual securities reports (有価証券報告書), earnings presentations, and analyst reports. Chain-of-thought fine-tuning: We generate step-by-step reasoning traces for financial QA tasks using a stronger teacher model, then distill these into our target VLM. Reinforcement learning from financial feedback: Domain experts provide preference signals on model outputs, which we use for RLHF-style optimization. Document Comprehension For robust document understanding, we focus on:
Layout-aware encoding: We integrate spatial position embeddings that capture the 2D structure of financial documents, enabling the model to correctly associate headers with their corresponding data cells in tables. OCR-free reading: Our architecture directly processes document images without relying on external OCR pipelines, reducing error propagation. Multi-page context: Financial documents often span dozens of pages. We implement an efficient attention mechanism that maintains context across page boundaries. Experiments We evaluate our model on several benchmarks:
Benchmark Description Metric JFinQA Japanese financial question answering Accuracy DocTabQA Table understanding in financial docs F1 FinRead-JP Reading comprehension on earnings reports ROUGE-L NumReason Numerical reasoning over financial data Exact Match Training Details Base model: A 7B parameter VLM pre-trained on a mixture of Japanese and English web data Financial pre-training: 50B tokens of Japanese financial text Fine-tuning: 100K instruction-response pairs with chain-of-thought annotations Hardware: 8× A100 GPUs, training completed in approximately 2 weeks Results Our model, which we call Compass, achieves state-of-the-art results across all four benchmarks:
JFinQA: 78.3% accuracy (+12.1% over the previous best) DocTabQA: 85.7 F1 (+8.4 over baseline) FinRead-JP: 71.2 ROUGE-L (+6.8 over baseline) NumReason: 64.5% exact match (+15.2% over baseline) The largest improvements come from numerical reasoning tasks, where our chain-of-thought training proves especially effective. The model demonstrates the ability to perform multi-step calculations involving currency conversion, percentage changes, and ratio analysis—capabilities that are critical for real-world financial analysis.
Ablation Study We conduct ablation studies to understand the contribution of each component:
Removing reasoning enhancement reduces JFinQA accuracy by 9.2% Removing layout-aware encoding reduces DocTabQA F1 by 11.3 Using external OCR instead of OCR-free reading introduces a 4.1% error rate increase Conclusion We have presented Compass, a Japanese financial VLM that integrates reasoning enhancement with document comprehension capabilities. Our results demonstrate that domain-specific training combined with architecture innovations can significantly improve performance on challenging financial document understanding tasks.
Future directions include extending the model to handle real-time market data, supporting longer document contexts, and exploring applications in automated financial reporting and compliance checking.
summary: We explore the development of a Vision-Language Model tailored for the Japanese financial domain, combining reasoning enhancement techniques with advanced document reading capabilities.
title: Developing a Japanese Financial VLM through Integrated Reasoning and Document Comprehension
